security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel ELF loader (load_elf_binary in fs/binfmt_elf.c) loads a RISC-V executable or shared library with GNU_PROPERTY_RISCV_FEATURE_1_AND containing CFI_LP_UNLABELED or CFI_SS bits set, but does not check for and enable the corresponding Zicfilp (landing pad) or Zicfiss/Zimop (shadow stack) hardware features before transferring control to userspace, nor does it refuse the load if hardware support is absent.
security_spec.summary: Kernel as the loader gatekeeper: if the kernel does not parse RISC-V .note.gnu.property CFI bits and enable Zicfilp/Zicfiss in {m,s}envcfg before delivering control to userspace, CFI-marked binaries execute with landing-pad checking and shadow-stack protection silently disabled, creating a false sense of security while ROP/JOP attacks remain viable

findings.finding: parse_elf_properties() gates on CONFIG_ARCH_USE_GNU_PROPERTY (line 790). RISC-V does not set this Kconfig, so GNU property parsing is a no-op on RISC-V. The PT_GNU_PROPERTY phdr is captured (lines 878-881, 980-981) and passed to parse_elf_properties() (line 994-995), but the function returns immediately without inspecting GNU_PROPERTY_RISCV_FEATURE_1_AND bits. This means CFI_LP_UNLABELED (Zicfilp) and CFI_SS (Zicfiss) bits in .note.gnu.property are never checked by the kernel ELF loader.

RISC-V uses the generic dummy arch_elf_pt_proc() because CONFIG_ARCH_BINFMT_ELF_STATE is not set. This stub returns 0 unconditionally — no PT_LOPROC..PT_HIPROC headers are inspected. However, this is by design: RISC-V CFI is managed via prctl() from userspace, not via ELF program header inspection at load time. The security guarantee is maintained at the prctl enablement gate, not at ELF load.

start_thread() correctly resets both shadow stack (Zicfiss) and landing pad (Zicfilp) state to disabled on every exec() via set_shstk_status(current, false) and set_indir_lp_status(current, false). This is the safe reset-before-userspace pattern: CFI starts off, and the dynamic linker (or static binary startup) must explicitly enable it via prctl. The prctl path in arch/riscv/kernel/usercfi.c guards enablement with cpu_supports_shadow_stack() and cpu_supports_indirect_br_lp_instr() hardware checks, so CFI cannot be enabled without hardware support.

RISC-V elf.h does not define ELF_PLAT_INIT, START_THREAD, or any CFI-related ELF property handling. No CONFIG_ARCH_USE_GNU_PROPERTY or CONFIG_ARCH_BINFMT_ELF_STATE is selected in arch/riscv/Kconfig. The architecture deliberately delegates CFI enablement to userspace via prctl(), consistent with the x86 CET model. The lack of ELF-load-time GNU property checking is a design choice, not an oversight.

The prctl enablement gates correctly check hardware support before allowing CFI features to be turned on. is_user_shstk_enabled() checks cpu_supports_shadow_stack() (Zicfiss). is_user_lpad_enabled() checks cpu_supports_indirect_br_lp_instr() (Zicfilp). These functions are called by arch_set_indir_br_lp_status() and arch_set_shadow_stack_status() respectively, which are the prctl handlers. Hardware-absent systems will reject CFI enablement via prctl, preventing userspace from running with CFI features that lack hardware backing.

GNU_PROPERTY_RISCV_FEATURE_1_AND and the ZICFILP/ZICFISS bit definitions (lines 99-102) are used exclusively for emitting .note.gnu.property in the VDSO (via vdso/note.S). The emit_riscv_feature_1_and macro is gated on VDSO_CFI && __riscv_xlen==64 (line 104). This is VDSO self-description, not kernel ELF-load-time policy. The VDSO accurately advertises the kernel's CFI capabilities. No vulnerability here.
findings.snippet:
#define GNU_PROPERTY_RISCV_FEATURE_1_AND 0xc0000000
#define GNU_PROPERTY_RISCV_FEATURE_1_ZICFILP      BIT(0)
#define GNU_PROPERTY_RISCV_FEATURE_1_ZICFISS      BIT(1)
#if defined(VDSO_CFI) && (__riscv_xlen == 64)
#define GNU_PROPERTY_RISCV_FEATURE_1_DEFAULT \
    (GNU_PROPERTY_RISCV_FEATURE_1_ZICFILP | GNU_PROPERTY_RISCV_FEATURE_1_ZICFISS)
